page.title: API Access
page.subtitle: Where Toskar's API is reachable, and how it is secured.

probe.notReady: Health check responded, but the service is not ready.
probe.unreachable: Could not reach the API on this computer.
probe.openaiDown: Service is up, but the OpenAI-compatible endpoint did not respond.
probe.needsKey: Responding. Other devices need a valid API key.
probe.checkFailed: Could not check the API — is the local service running?

service.title: Service
service.lanHint: Use this computer's LAN IP with port <mono>{{port}}</mono> (for example <mono>http://192.168.x.x:{{port}}/v1</mono>).
service.docsBody: Toskar exposes an OpenAI-compatible API at <mono>/v1</mono>. Point clients at the endpoint above and send <header/> when Toskar is reachable from other computers. `/api/v1` and `/v1` both require that header. A key does not encrypt plain HTTP.

lan.title: Local network access
lan.on: Devices on your local network can connect using an API key.
lan.off: Only apps on this computer can use Toskar’s API.
lan.noKeys: Network access is on, but there are no API keys yet. Create a key before connecting from another device.
lan.notes: Changes apply right away. Other devices need an API key; apps on this computer don't. A key does not encrypt traffic on plain HTTP. Test API only checks this computer — not reachability from other devices.
lan.confirmBody: Devices on your local network will be able to connect to Toskar. An API key is required for all remote connections.
lan.confirmHttp: An API key over plain HTTP does not encrypt traffic.
lan.browserKey: Create an API key so this browser can keep connecting after the server rebinds. The full key is shown only once.

keys.title: API keys
keys.description: Credentials for apps and devices that talk to Toskar.
keys.createHint: Give this key a name so you know what uses it.
keys.copyNow: Copy this secret now — it won't be shown again
keys.confirmRotate: Rotate “{{name}}”? The old secret stops working immediately.
keys.confirmRevoke: Revoke “{{name}}”? Apps using this key will lose access.

permissions.note: Requests can ask for less, never more. Over the network these limits always apply; on this computer they apply when the app sends this key.

share.title: Use Toskar in other AI apps
share.description: Apps that support MCP can ask your local AI, list its models, and search your connected knowledge. Answers stay on your computers, and the local AI only uses tools that read.
share.needsKey: Toskar is open to your network, so apps need an API key. Create one below and put it where the settings say <key/>. The key's permissions apply.

where.claudeDesktop: In Claude Desktop, open Settings → Developer → Edit Config, add this, and restart Claude.
where.cursor: Add this to ~/.cursor/mcp.json (Cursor Settings → MCP → Add new global MCP server).
where.vscode: Run "MCP: Open User Configuration" from the Command Palette and add this.
where.other: Apps that connect to MCP servers by address use Streamable HTTP at this address. Apps that start a program use the command instead.

phones.title: Devices
phones.description: Phones, tablets, and TVs connected with a code. Each has its own key, which can chat and read lists but can't change this computer.
phones.confirmDisconnect: Disconnect {{name}}? It will need a new code to connect again.
